disagreements.topic: EV/EBITDA basis: 10x NTM (agents 1, 5) / 10.5x FY28E (agent 2) / 11.1x horizon TTM (agent 3) / 12.4x horizon TTM (agent 4)
disagreements.positions: Agents 1, 2, 3 and 5 land their EV/EBITDA legs at $331-343. Agent_4 takes 20% off MasTec's trailing EV/EBITDA (Finviz 15.47x) to get 12.4x and applies it to horizon-TTM EBITDA of $1,097M, for a $367 leg that is $25 above its own P/E leg ($342).
disagreements.resolution: Settled on a forward basis: NTM company-adjusted EBITDA less lease-inclusive net debt, at 10x in the round-2 reconciliation (about 10.6x FY28E, which is the current year at the horizon) and 9.5x after the post-gate decision (about 10.1x FY28E; see post_gate_decisions). MasTec's trailing multiple overstates the anchor because its EBITDA is growing fast. Its FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guide is $1,600M against $1,150.1M in FY2025, so on a filings-based EV of $20.12B (Oct-9 close $212.65 x 80.30M shares on the Q2 10-Q cover + $2,740.2M debt incl. finance leases + $495.2M operating leases - $315.6M cash + $123.0M NCI) MTZ trades at 12.6x its current-year guide but 14.6x its company-adjusted TTM EBITDA ($1,379.5M = 1,150.1 + 667.9 - 438.5). On that current-year basis a 16x NTM P/E (equity ~$10.37B + $2.56B lease-inclusive net debt = EV ~$12.93B) is ~10.6x FY28E EBITDA of ~$1.218B, about 15.6% below MTZ's 12.57x (10.61 / 12.57 = 0.844); the reconciled 15x (equity ~$9.72B, EV ~$12.28B) is ~10.1x FY28E, about 20% below (10.08 / 12.57 = 0.802). Agent_4's 12.4x trailing multiple works out to ~11.1x FY28E (EV $13.58B / $1.22B), only ~11% below MTZ, which is roughly a 17x P/E and the same over-generosity the round-1 review corrected from 17x to 16x. Corrected, agent_4's EV leg is ~$344 and its blend ~$343. Agents 2 and 3 (10.5x FY28E; 11.1x horizon TTM, which is ~10x NTM) are consistent with 10x NTM. [Citation gate 2026-10-12] MTZ multiples re-derived from filings; the earlier 12.4x / 15.1x used StockAnalysis EV $19.78B and vendor EBITDA, which the gate does not accept for peer multiples.
disagreements.evidence: MasTec Q2 2026 release on SEC (FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guide $1,600M; FY2025 $1,150.1M; H1 2026 $667.9M vs H1 2025 $438.5M; Jun-30 debt $2,740.2M, cash $315.6M); MasTec Q2 10-Q XBRL (80,304,948 shares at Jul 27, 2026; operating lease liabilities $495.2M; NCI $123.0M); Yahoo chart Oct-9 close $212.65. Ratios are estimates from these figures. Vendor ratios (StockAnalysis EV $19.78B / 15.12x; Finviz 15.47x) are superseded.

disagreements.topic: Horizon net debt and the buyback authorization
disagreements.positions: Agent_5 says the buyback authorization expired 2026-08-25 with $83.9M unused, so it assumes no buybacks and $2.30B. Agent_2 removed the 'new buyback' as unverified, also $2.30B. Agent_1 cites $83.9M left plus a new $150M program, $2.34B. Agent_3 has $2.33B. Agent_4 has $2.50B lease-inclusive. All agents now add the ~$0.23B of leases.
disagreements.resolution: Settled at the 10-Q. Note 23 (Subsequent Events): on Aug 26, 2026 the Board authorized a new $150.0M repurchase program through February 2028. It replaces the $83.9M left under the prior program (which ran through Aug 25, 2026), and the full $150.0M was available at Aug 27, 2026. Agent_5's 'no current authorization' and agent_2's 'unverified' are wrong. Starting point (10-Q / Q2 deck): cash $340.1M, carrying debt $2,819.7M ($28.4M current + $2,791.3M long-term), notional net debt $2,502.6M, operating lease liabilities $228.7M. Reconciled horizon: $2.33B notional (estimate: 2,502.6 - ~250 underlying FCF + ~75 buybacks), so $2.56B lease-inclusive. Leases are subtracted only because the EV/EBITDA anchor is benchmarked on lease-inclusive EVs (MTZ's filings-based EV includes $495.2M of operating leases; StockAnalysis total debt for DY is $3.05B = $2.82B carrying + ~$0.23B leases). The buyback assumption is close to neutral per share: $75M adds ~$2.5/share of net debt but retires ~0.26M shares at ~$290.
disagreements.evidence: 10-Q dy-20260801, Note 17, Note 23, balance sheet and lease note ($228.7M); Q2 FY27 presentation 'Notional Net Debt $2,502.6'; XBRL OperatingLeaseLiability 228,725,000 at 2026-08-01.

disagreements.topic: FY28 EPS haircut and FY29 growth (FY29 consensus is paywalled)
disagreements.positions: FY28 haircuts: agent_5 -3%, agent_2 -4%, agents 1 and 4 -5% (applied to NTM), agent_3 -9% (bottom-up $18.96). FY29 growth: +9% (a3), +10% (a2, a5), +12% (a1, a4). NTM EPS at the horizon ranges $20.26-21.55, worth ~$20/share at 16x.
disagreements.resolution: I use FY28 = $20.78 x 0.96 = $19.95 and FY29 = +11% = $22.14, so calendar-weighted NTM (0.31/0.69) is $21.46. The 4% haircut (the median of the agents) rests on two verified items: the Communications margin outlook turned to 'slight decline' (Q2 release), and implied H2 FY27 Communications revenue is roughly flat. Consensus was still $20.78 after the August print (11 analysts, StockAnalysis), so there is no verified downward revision. Agent_3's -9% is a defensible skeptic build but rests on its own margin assumptions (Communications 13.2%, Building Systems 19%), not on a reported datapoint, so it is not adopted. FY29 +11% sits below FY28 consensus revenue growth (+13.2%) and is supported by a $12.24B backlog (+53.2%) with $6.47B due in the next 12 months ($5,362M Communications + $1,110M Building Systems). Agent_3's earnings-weighted 0.24/0.76 split is technically defensible because Q4 is seasonally small; it would add ~$0.15 of NTM EPS (~$2/share at 15x), which is immaterial.
disagreements.evidence: StockAnalysis DY forecast (FY27 $17.05 / FY28 $20.78 EPS, FY28 revenue $8.58B, FY29 'Pro' locked, 11 analysts); Q2 FY27 release (outlook text, backlog table).

disagreements.topic: Covenant: is the 3.50x senior secured test a default trigger? (agent_3 vs round-1 supervisor)
disagreements.positions: Round-1 supervisor said the 3.50x figure 'could not be verified'. Agent_3 found it in the 10-Q and says it only caps incremental facilities.
disagreements.resolution: Agent_3 is right, and the round-1 supervisor's 'unverified' label is withdrawn. The 10-Q states that incremental facilities may be added up to $927.0M plus any amount that keeps the consolidated senior secured net leverage ratio at or below 3.50x pro forma. That is an incurrence cap on new debt, not a maintenance test. The maintenance covenants are maximum consolidated net leverage of 4.50x, stepping to 4.00x after the first fiscal quarter ending after Dec 23, 2027 (about FYE Jan-2028, i.e. after the horizon), and minimum interest coverage of 2.50x. The company was in compliance at Aug 1, 2026 with $746.4M of revolver availability. Covenant stress is not a thesis-break channel. The 3.50x cap matters only as a limit on further debt-funded M&A.
disagreements.evidence: 10-Q dy-20260801, Note 14 (Debt), credit agreement description and liquidity section.

disagreements.topic: The '~$10M underlying' Communications guide cut (agent_4 did not reopen the Q1 release)
disagreements.positions: Agents 1, 2, 3 and 5 accept ~$150M deferral + ~$10M underlying. Agent_4 kept it out of its numbers as not personally verified.
disagreements.resolution: Verified at both releases. Q1 FY27 (May 27, 2026) raised the FY27 Communications outlook to $6.03-6.20B (midpoint $6.115B) and expected 'modest' Communications margin improvement. Q2 FY27 (Aug 26, 2026) set $5.90-6.01B (midpoint $5.955B), 'reflects the deferral of approximately $150 million of wireless program revenues into fiscal 2028. Overall program scope is unchanged', and now expects a 'slight decline' in Communications margin. Midpoint change -$160M, less ~$150M deferral = ~-$10M underlying (estimate). The March initial guide was $5.70-5.90B (Q4 FY26 release). Agent_4 may use it.
disagreements.evidence: Q1 FY27, Q2 FY27 and Q4 FY26 earnings releases (8-K EX-99.1).

disagreements.topic: Agent_5's base rates on Yahoo chart URLs
disagreements.positions: Agent_5 rebuilt its base rates on query1.finance.yahoo.com v8 chart URLs: DY's 12-month forward median when >=45% below its 12-month high is -8.5% (36% positive, n=36); unconditional +15.6% / 63%; pooled peer episodes +14.8%, 8 of 14 positive; 2018 analog $83.91 -> $44.50.
disagreements.resolution: The URLs reopen with no key (HTTP 200 JSON, no login). On that data I reproduced DY's conditional rate exactly (n=36, median -8.5%, 36.1% positive), the unconditional 63.2% positive (median +15.3% vs agent_5's +15.6%), the 2018 analog (Aug-2018 close $83.91 to Aug-2019 $44.50) and realized vol (1y 52.3%, 3m 56.2%, 1m 43.3%). I could not reproduce the pooled peer-episode statistic. A simple first-month-of-drawdown definition across DY, MTZ, PWR, EME, FIX, PRIM and MYRG gives 27 episodes, median +32.9%, 18 of 27 positive. The result is definition-sensitive. DY's own conditional sample is ~3 independent episodes (2001-02, 2008-09, 2018-19) counted in overlapping months. Base rates therefore span 36-67% positive and give no directional edge, which supports staying at the mean.
disagreements.evidence: Yahoo v8 chart monthly series for DY, MTZ, PWR, EME, FIX, PRIM, MYRG and DY daily 2y (reopened 2026-10-12).

disagreements.topic: Peer-set size (rule asks for 10-12; agents use 8, 9, 11)
disagreements.positions: Agents 2 and 5 use 8 peers; agent_3 uses 9 (keeps LMB); agent_1 uses 11 (keeps GVA, AGX, LMB for the 10-12 rule); agent_4 uses 11 on Finviz with an 8-core median.
disagreements.resolution: Reconciled set: 8 peers (MTZ, PWR, PRIM, MYRG, EME, FIX, IESC, STRL), as a documented exception to the 10-12 rule. These are the listed US specialty contractors with telecom, utility or data-center electrical exposure at scale. GVA (civil/paving) and AGX (power-plant EPC, net cash $1.02B) are different businesses. LMB ($611M market cap, mechanical/HVAC) is a weaker Building Systems analogue than EME, FIX and IESC, which are already included. Padding to 11 moves the forward P/E median only from 22.0x to 21.6x (gate-derived: Oct-9 close / calendarised NTM consensus EPS; IESC has no consensus page and is left out of the P/E median), so the exception is immaterial to fair value. All agents use the same 16x target, which is ~12% below MTZ's 18.2x NTM P/E and ~27% below the 22.0x peer median. After the gate the reconciled target is 15x (~17.5% below MTZ's 18.18x, ~32% below the 22.01x median; see post_gate_decisions).
disagreements.evidence: Gate re-derivation 2026-10-12: Yahoo chart Oct-9 closes; StockAnalysis forecast pages (S&P Global consensus EPS this/next year); each peer's latest 10-Q/10-K XBRL (cover shares, debt incl. finance leases, operating leases, cash, NCI, TTM operating income + D&A). Vendor ratios on StockAnalysis statistics pages and Finviz v=121/v=152 are superseded.

disagreements.positions: Agent_1 keeps a 10%-weight FCF leg at 60% underlying conversion and a 6% yield ($208). The other agents dropped FCF legs.
disagreements.resolution: Dropped from the reconciled value. The cash-quality problem (supplier-finance $0 -> $367.4M; FY26 AP increase $223.2M) is already one of the three reasons agent_1 gives for its 16x P/E discount, so a separate FCF leg priced at a 6% yield counts it twice. It is also on an FY28 basis, not the horizon NTM. Without it, agent_1's blend is ~$337 (0.556 x 342 + 0.444 x 331).
disagreements.evidence: XBRL SupplierFinanceProgramObligation (0; 226.4M; 349.4M; 367.4M) and IncreaseDecreaseInAccountsPayable FY26 223,234,000; agent_1 comps_summary.

one_month_reasoning: No Dycom earnings fall in the window. Q3 releases came on 2025-11-19, 2024-11-20, 2023-11-21 and 2022-11-22 (EDGAR), so Q3 FY27 is likely Nov 18-25. The in-window events are verified and non-directional: Loudoun's Oct 20 vote on an up-to-12-month pause of legislative data-center/substation approvals (retroactive to Sep 15, administrative processes unaffected), the Oct 27-28 FOMC (hike 15.5% Kalshi / 16.5% Polymarket), carrier Q3 reports after the Oct 9 SpaceX-Grain spectrum shock (carriers -5.5% to -7.4% premarket, towers +6.7% to +8.3%), and peer Q3 prints. So I keep the forecasters' near-symmetric mean (P(>=269.23) = 0.498), which uses ~15% monthly sigma; realized vol is 43% over 1 month and 56% over 3 months.
confidence_reason: Round-2 checks settled every factual dispute: the buyback is re-authorized, the covenant is an incurrence cap, the $10M underlying cut is verified, the Yahoo base rates reopen, and the peer multiples were re-derived from filings at the citation gate. The agents' corrections offset: agent_4's EV leg comes down (~$352 -> ~$343), agent_1's double-counted FCF leg comes out (~$324 -> ~$337), and the buyback fix is roughly per-share neutral, for a corrected agent mean of ~$338. After the gate I cut the reconciled multiples from 16x to 15x NTM P/E and from 10x to 9.5x NTM EV/EBITDA, because on the gate's figures 16x was only ~12% below MTZ's 18.18x while the leverage, cash-quality and concentration reasons are unchanged or worse (post_gate_decisions). My reconciled fair value ($322) is therefore ~5% below the corrected agent mean, and the whole gap is that multiple judgment. The ladders were not re-fitted in this post-gate step and still reflect the forecasters' mean (median ~$292; P(>=323) = 0.402).
thesis_break_reason: $200 is 9.3x my horizon NTM EPS ($21.46), 10.0x my haircut FY28 EPS ($19.95), 9.6x the $20.78 consensus, and 24% below the $263.36 52-week low. A close there would mean an earnings reset, not 52%-vol noise. Channels: an FY28 outlook (early Mar-2027) with Communications declining even after the ~$150M wireless recapture; an AT&T/Verizon program cut (30.5% of Q2 revenue together); Building Systems backlog ($1,110M next-12-month) shrinking as DMV legislative pauses reach awards; or the $367.4M supplier-finance balance reversing and pulling FCF negative. Covenant breach is not a channel: maintenance is 4.50x net leverage and 2.50x interest coverage, with $746.4M of revolver availability; the 3.50x senior secured figure only caps incremental debt.
key_drivers: Is H2 FY27 Communications flatness timing or a cycle peak? The FY27 Communications midpoint fell $160M (May $6.115B -> Aug $5.955B), of which ~$150M is a stated wireless deferral into FY28 and ~$10M is underlying, and the margin outlook flipped from 'modest improvement' to 'slight decline'. The early-March 2027 FY28 outlook decides it.

The fall was a de-rating, not an estimate cut. FY28 consensus is still $20.78 (11 analysts). DY trades at 13.7x NTM consensus EPS against MTZ at 18.2x and a 7-peer median of 22.0x (gate-derived), and a persistent discount to MTZ (15x NTM P/E, ~17.5% below MTZ's 18.18x and ~21% below it on the unhaircut EPS path; 9.5x NTM EV/EBITDA, ~10.1x FY28E, ~20% below MTZ's 12.57x current-year multiple) is justified by leverage (2.82x vs 2.12x lease-inclusive net debt / company-adjusted TTM EBITDA; 3.20x for DY if the $367.4M supplier-finance balance is counted as debt), concentration and cash quality.

Cash quality and leverage: notional net debt $2,502.6M, and supplier-finance obligations went $0 -> $367.4M in 12 months (FY26 AP +$223.2M). H1 FY27 FCF was -$54.2M. The Q3 10-Q (late Nov) shows whether the build continues or unwinds. A new $150M buyback (through Feb-2028) is available but small.

Carrier concentration: AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4%, Lumen 5.3% of Q2 revenue. Verizon guides 2026 capex down $0.5-1bn while AT&T targets 40M fiber locations by end-2026 and 60M by 2030. The SpaceX-Grain 800 MHz deal hit carriers and lifted towers, a mixed read.
Rates: Kalshi/Polymarket price a ~73% chance of a December hike, a headwind for levered, de-rated contractors.

fair_value.reason: P/E leg (60%): NTM adjusted EPS at 2027-10-09 = 0.31 x FY28 $19.95 ($20.78 consensus x 0.96) + 0.69 x FY29 $22.14 (+11%) = $21.46; x 15.0x (judgment, cut from 16x after the citation gate; see post_gate_decisions) = $322. On the gate-derived multiples 15x is ~17.5% below MTZ's 18.18x NTM consensus P/E (15 / 18.18 = 0.825), ~18% below the 18.36x telecom-core (MTZ, PRIM) average and ~32% below the 22.01x 7-peer median; because the EPS it is applied to is 4% below consensus it equals 14.4x on the unhaircut EPS path, ~21% below MTZ like for like (14.4 / 18.18 = 0.792). EV/EBITDA leg (40%): FY28 EBITDA $8.58B x 14.2% = $1.218B; FY29 +9% = $1.328B; NTM = 0.31 x 1.218 + 0.69 x 1.328 = $1.294B; x 9.5x (judgment, cut from 10x so that the leg matches the 15x P/E) = EV $12.29B (~10.1x FY28E, ~20% below MTZ's 12.57x EV on its $1,600M 2026 guide), less lease-inclusive horizon net debt of $2.56B ($2.33B notional + $0.229B operating leases) = $9.73B / 30.2M shares = $322. Blend 0.6 x 322 + 0.4 x 322 = $322 (estimate). The forecasters' fair values (mean $337) move to ~$338 after my round-2 corrections: agent_4 ~$343 (EV leg at 10x NTM), agent_1 ~$337 (FCF leg removed), agents 2, 3 and 5 unchanged within $1 (buyback fix per-share neutral). All five keep 16x, so the reconciled value is ~5% below that corrected mean, and the gap is the multiple judgment alone. All inputs are verified at the Q2 release, the 10-Q, XBRL and StockAnalysis consensus (re-opened by the citation gate 2026-10-12); the multiples, haircut and FY29 growth are judgment.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.basis: NTM company-adjusted EBITDA at 2027-10-09, $1.294B; lease-inclusive net debt $2.56B; 30.2M shares

comps_review.spot_checks: Citation gate 2026-10-12: vendor page ratios (StockAnalysis 'Forward PE' and EV/EBITDA; Finviz v=121/v=152) were reopened and match what the agents quoted, but peer multiples and leverage must come from filings, so every ratio was re-derived. Forward P/E = Oct-9 close (Yahoo chart) / NTM consensus EPS (StockAnalysis this-year/next-year S&P Global estimates, weights 0.227/0.773 for Dec FYE; AGX 0.312/0.688; DY 0.31/0.69). EV = close x 10-Q cover shares (IESC x2 for the Aug-2026 2:1 split) + debt incl. finance leases + operating lease liabilities - cash and short-term investments + NCI (latest 10-Q XBRL); EBITDA = TTM GAAP operating income + D&A (10-K/10-Q XBRL), except MTZ and DY on company-adjusted TTM EBITDA from their releases. Fwd P/E / EV/EBITDA: MTZ 18.18 / 14.58, PWR 37.00 / 36.64, PRIM 18.54 / 17.68 (TTM depressed by a Q2-2026 operating loss), MYRG 22.20 / 16.19, EME 22.01 / 16.13, FIX 29.77 / 29.38, IESC n/a (no consensus page) / 20.97, STRL 21.21 / 22.51, LMB 11.40 / 11.25, GVA 14.34 / 11.58, AGX 25.79 / 24.25; DY 13.72 / 11.28 (EV $10.83B, adjusted TTM EBITDA $959.8M). Leverage (lease-inclusive net debt / company-adjusted TTM EBITDA): DY 2.82x ($2,708.3M / $959.8M), MTZ 2.12x ($2,919.8M / $1,379.5M); ex leases 2.58x vs 1.76x.
dropped_peers: LMB (sub-$1B mechanical; weaker Building Systems analogue than EME/FIX/IESC)
comps_review.peer_count_exception: 8 peers, below the 10-12 rule: there are not 10 genuinely comparable listed US specialty contractors with DY's telecom/utility/data-center mix. Padding to 11 (adding GVA, AGX, LMB) moves the gate-derived median forward P/E from 22.01x to 21.61x and does not change any agent's target multiple.
comps_review.target_multiple: 15.0x NTM adjusted EPS (judgment, cut from 16x after the citation gate: ~17.5% below MTZ's 18.18x, ~18% below the 18.36x telecom-core average and ~32% below the 22.01x 7-peer median, gate-derived; applied to EPS 4% below consensus, so ~21% below MTZ on the unhaircut EPS path); 9.5x NTM adjusted EBITDA with lease-inclusive net debt (cut from 10x to match the P/E leg; ~10.1x FY28E, ~20% below MTZ's 12.57x EV on its $1,600M 2026 guide, filings-based EV). The 16x / 10x pair it replaces was ~12% / ~15.5% below MTZ on the same figures.
comps_review.discount_justification: The discount is persistent and verified. Leverage: lease-inclusive net debt / company-adjusted TTM EBITDA 2.82x for DY ($2,819.7M debt + $228.7M leases - $340.1M cash = $2,708.3M over $959.8M) vs 2.12x for MTZ ($2,919.8M over $1,379.5M); 2.58x vs 1.76x excluding leases (10-Qs, Q2 releases). Several high-multiple peers (EME, FIX, IESC, STRL, MYRG) hold net cash (10-Qs). Concentration: 35.8% of Q2 revenue from three carriers. Cash quality: a $367.4M supplier-finance build (~$12/share or ~0.6 of a P/E turn if treated as debt; counted as debt it takes DY's lease-inclusive leverage to 3.20x) and H1 FY27 FCF of -$54.2M even with +$141.0M of that build. Together these support a discount to MTZ of about 20% like for like (15x on haircut EPS = 14.4x on the unhaircut path vs 18.18x; 9.5x NTM EV/EBITDA = ~10.1x FY28E vs 12.57x), not the ~12% that 16x gives on the gate's figures; see post_gate_decisions. Agent_4's 12.4x trailing EV/EBITDA is too generous (~11.1x FY28E, ~11% below MTZ's 12.6x on a current-year basis, inconsistent with its own 16x P/E) and is corrected to 10x NTM. The other agents' multiples are within tolerance.
comps_review.reconciled_peer_median_fwd_pe_note: Median of 7 (IESC has no consensus EPS source); Oct-9 close / calendarised NTM consensus EPS. Including Finviz's 22.0x for IESC would leave it at 22.0x.

Round-2 checks found the agents' remaining disputes small and offsetting: a new $150M buyback exists, the 3.50x covenant is only an incurrence cap, agent_4's trailing EV/EBITDA was too generous, and agent_1 double-counted cash quality. Reconciled fair value is ~$322 (15x NTM EPS $21.46; 9.5x NTM EBITDA). After the citation gate, 16x was only ~12% below MasTec's 18.18x, less than the leverage, cash-quality and concentration reasons support, so I cut it (post_gate_decisions). That puts fair value ~5% below the corrected agent mean of ~$338; the mean ladder (P>=269 = 0.58) was not re-fitted in this step, and confidence stays low. The decisive event is the early-March 2027 FY28 outlook, and the Q3 10-Q in late November is the first read on whether the supplier-finance build unwinds.

post_gate_decisions.reason: Judgment, 2026-10-12, after the citation gate. 16x was set as 'about 20% below MasTec' on a vendor 19.89x. On the gate's basis MTZ is 18.18x NTM ($212.65 / $11.70), so 16x is only 12% below it (16 / 18.18 = 0.880); a literal 20% would be 14.5x (0.80 x 18.18). The re-measurement lowered every comparator by 5-9% (MTZ 19.89 -> 18.18, -8.6%; 7-peer median 23.29 -> 22.01, -5.5%; DY itself 14.60 -> 13.72, -6.0%) because the gate's NTM EPS is further forward, which is the same basis as the $21.46 the target is applied to. Keeping 16x would raise the target against every comparator although the gate found no fact in DY's favour (16 x 0.940 = 15.0x; 16 x 0.945 = 15.1x). The sourced discount reasons are unchanged or worse: lease-inclusive net debt / company-adjusted TTM EBITDA is 2.82x for DY vs 2.12x for MTZ, or 3.20x for DY if the $367.4M supplier-finance balance is counted as debt ($3,075.7M / $959.8M). That balance alone is ~$12.2/share (367.4 / 30.2), ~0.57 of a P/E turn (12.2 / 21.46), ~3% of MTZ's multiple. H1 FY27 FCF was -$54.2M even with a +$141.0M supplier-finance build (~-$195M without it), and 35.8% of Q2 revenue came from AT&T, Verizon and Lumen. Together these support a like-for-like discount of about 20%, not 12%. I stop at 15x rather than 14.5x because the multiple is applied to EPS already cut 4% for the Communications margin and flat-H2 risk, which is how carrier concentration reaches earnings. 15x on haircut EPS = 14.4x on the unhaircut path, 20.8% below MTZ's consensus-based 18.18x; 14.5x would be 13.9x, 23.4% below, counting that risk twice (the reason agent_1's FCF leg was dropped). 15x is 17.5% below MTZ on the raw multiple, ~18% below the 18.36x telecom-core average and 31.8% below the 22.01x median. P/E leg: 15 x $21.46 = $322 (was $343).

Judgment, 2026-10-12. The stated '~16% below MTZ's 12.6x' for 10x NTM is 15.5% on the gate's figures: 10x x $1.294B = EV $12.94B = 10.62x FY28E EBITDA of $1.218B, vs MTZ's 12.57x ($20.12B filings-based EV / $1,600M 2026 guide); 10.62 / 12.57 = 0.845. 10x NTM is the EV multiple a 16x P/E implies (16 x $21.46 x 30.2M + $2.56B = $12.93B), so with the P/E at 15x the EV leg moves too, keeping the legs consistent as agent_4 was asked to do. 15x implies EV $12.28B = 9.49x NTM. At 9.5x NTM, EV is $12.29B = 10.09x FY28E, 19.7% below MTZ's 12.57x, the same ~20% like-for-like discount. Supplier finance and concentration are not in net debt, so they belong in the EV multiple as well. EV leg: (12.29 - 2.56) / 30.2M = $322 (was $344).

0.6 x $322 (15x x $21.46) + 0.4 x $322 (9.5x NTM EBITDA) = $322. A literal 20%-below-MTZ P/E (14.5x, $311) with the EV leg left at 10x ($344) would blend to ~$324, but that pairs a 14.5x P/E with an EV leg that implies 16x; made consistent (9.24x NTM) it would be $311. $322 is ~5% below the corrected agent mean (~$338), because all five agents keep 16x. Ladders, thesis break ($200 = 9.3x NTM EPS, unchanged) and sizing numbers are not changed in this step; the current ladder has P(>=323) = 0.402 and a median of ~$292. The citation_audit block above is the gate's dated record, written before this decision, so its 'fair value $343 unchanged' refers to the gate step.
